# UI art prompts — Chaos Arena (generated by art/ui/build.mjs — do not edit by hand)

The stat icons (team upgrade screen, in-battle stat cards, power-up boxes) and the power-up boxes.
Until a set is painted the game draws its own fallback (the SVG stat icons, renderPowerup).
Paint the STAT ICONS first: the power-up box prompt attaches the painted icon sheet as a finish reference.

Paint: attach the finish references listed under a heading FIRST, the layout reference LAST, then paste ONLY the fenced block.
Or `pnpm art:desk` → search the sprite name → Copy image, then prompt. Returns are sliced by art/ui/slice-return.mjs.

## Stat icons — attack, defense, speed, HP, weight, level-up  (ui-stat-icons.png → images/stats/attack_256x256.webp)

Attach, in this order: `public/images/icons/coin_128x128.webp`, then `art-sheets/ui/ui-stat-icons.png` LAST.

```text
WHAT COMES BACK IS ONE SHEET OF SIX GAME ICONS IN A 3 x 2 GRID, ON FLAT MAGENTA.
One landscape image, 1536 x 1024 pixels: three icons in the top row, three in the bottom row, each one centred in its own invisible 512 x 512 square, exactly where the grey shapes sit in the LAST attached image.
· 6 separate icons. Not 5, not 7, not one combined emblem, not a scene.

WHAT THE ATTACHMENTS ARE — read this before anything else.
· The LAST attachment is the LAYOUT REFERENCE: six flat grey silhouettes on magenta. They are NOTATION: they fix each icon's SUBJECT, POSITION and SIZE. Take nothing else from them — not their grey, not their flat fills, not their exact outline. A result that comes back as the same grey shapes neatly shaded is a trace of the placeholder, and it is unusable.
· The FIRST attachment is a FINISH REFERENCE: the game's gold coin. Copy its finish — the bold dark outline, the glossy cel shading, the warm highlight, the level of detail — and NEVER its subject: no coin, no star.

WHAT IT IS — the stat icons of "Chaos Arena", a spinning-top battle game. They stand next to numbers on the team-upgrade screen and the in-battle stat cards, at 16 to 60 pixels across, and the same icons are stamped on the power-up boxes the blades collect in the arena. Each must say its stat at a glance.

READ THE PANELS — left to right, top row first:
· Panel 1 (top row, left) — ATTACK: a short, broad steel sword pointing to the top-right at 45 degrees, with a red cross-guard and a red wrapped grip; a hot red edge glint runs along the blade. Colour: fiery red (#ef4444 body, #fca5a5 highlights, #7f1d1d shadows).
· Panel 2 (top row, middle) — DEFENSE: a heater shield (flat top, pointed bottom) in blue enamel with a thick polished steel rim and four rivets, a lighter blue chevron across its face. Colour: royal blue (#3b82f6 body, #93c5fd highlights, #1e3a8a shadows).
· Panel 3 (top row, right) — SPEED: a fat zig-zag lightning bolt leaning to the right, trailed on its left by three short horizontal motion streaks of the same colour. Colour: electric cyan (#22d3ee body, #a5f3fc highlights, #155e75 shadows).
· Panel 4 (bottom row, left) — HP: a plump glossy heart with a bold white plus sign in its middle. Colour: emerald green (#22c55e body, #86efac highlights, #14532d shadows).
· Panel 5 (bottom row, middle) — WEIGHT: a heavy iron dumbbell lying horizontally — two big round plates on each end, a knurled bar between them. Colour: gunmetal steel grey (#94a3b8 body, #e2e8f0 highlights, #334155 shadows).
· Panel 6 (bottom row, right) — LEVEL UP: one thick, chunky upward arrow (a wide triangular head on a short broad shaft), like an "upgrade" button glyph. Colour: bright lime green (#84cc16 body, #d9f99d highlights, #365314 shadows) with a gold (#facc15) rim.

THE VIEW — flat and frontal, like a sticker. No perspective, no tilt, no cast shadow.

CONSISTENCY — one artist, one set: the same outline weight, the same shading steps, the same light direction and the same visual size in every panel. Each icon fills its square evenly: about 380 px across its longest side, centred.

STYLE — polished mobile-game UI art, like the finish reference (the game's gold coin):
· A bold, dark navy-black contour (#0f1a30) around every object — at its heaviest about 4% of the object's width. It must survive being shrunk to 20 pixels: if it reads as a hairline, it is several times too thin.
· Rich, saturated colour with two or three cel-shading steps per shape, light from the top-left, and a crisp white highlight painted ON glossy and metal surfaces (a shine band or dot — never a four-pointed sparkle star floating beside it).
· Chunky, simple, instantly readable silhouettes: every object must still read at 20 pixels across, on a dark navy UI and on a bright blue button alike — high contrast against both.
· AVOID: flat vector clip-art; thin lines and fine detail that turns to mush when small; photorealism or a plastic 3D render; text, letters, numbers or runes; drop shadows; anything see-through.

LAYOUT / SIZE — measured against the image, not judged by eye:
· Each icon is centred in its 512 x 512 square and about 380 px across its longest side (74% of the square) — as big as its grey silhouette.
· At least 60 px of magenta between every icon and its square's edges, so no two icons touch.
· The bottom-right corner of the image stays empty magenta.

BACKGROUND — this matters more than the style.
Fill every pixel that is not art with solid, flat, pure magenta #FF00FF, edge to edge — treat it as a green screen.
· EXACTLY #FF00FF — red 255, green 0, blue 255. Not pink, not purple, not a tinted version of it.
· NOT transparent (never a grey-and-white checkerboard), NOT white, NOT a gradient, NOT a texture.
· No card, tile, plate, circle or frame behind any object; no grid lines or panel borders; no glow, halo or shadow on the magenta. Any glow stays INSIDE the object's outline.
· No object contains magenta or hot pink anywhere.

BEFORE YOU CALL IT FINISHED, count and check:
· Exactly six icons, three per row: sword, shield, lightning bolt / heart with plus, dumbbell, up arrow.
· Each in its stat colour: red, blue, cyan / green, steel grey, lime green with gold.
· Every icon has the same thick dark outline.
· Every pixel that is not an icon is flat, vivid #FF00FF.
· No text, numbers, sparkle stars, panel borders or watermarks.

OUTPUT: one image, 1536 x 1024 pixels, 3:2 landscape, PNG. If your tool has an aspect-ratio control, set it to 3:2. No labels, captions, numbers or watermarks.
```

## Power-up boxes — attack, defense, speed  (ui-power-up-boxes.png → images/powerups/attack-box_256x256.webp)

```text

One square image, 1024 x 1024 pixels, split into four invisible 512 x 512 squares: a box in the top-left, the top-right and the bottom-left square, each centred exactly where the grey box sits in the LAST attached image. The BOTTOM-RIGHT square stays EMPTY flat magenta.

READ THE PANELS:

· Panel 2 (top-right) — the DEFENSE box: its energy colour is royal blue (#3b82f6 body, #93c5fd highlights, #1e3a8a shadows).

CONSISTENCY — the three boxes are the SAME box in three colours: same shape, same size, same brackets, same plate, same lighting. Only the energy colour changes.

STYLE — polished mobile-game UI art, like the finish reference (the game's gold coin):
· A bold, dark navy-black contour (#0f1a30) around every object — at its heaviest about 4% of the object's width. It must survive being shrunk to 20 pixels: if it reads as a hairline, it is several times too thin.
· Rich, saturated colour with two or three cel-shading steps per shape, light from the top-left, and a crisp white highlight painted ON glossy and metal surfaces (a shine band or dot — never a four-pointed sparkle star floating beside it).
· Chunky, simple, instantly readable silhouettes: every object must still read at 20 pixels across, on a dark navy UI and on a bright blue button alike — high contrast against both.
· AVOID: flat vector clip-art; thin lines and fine detail that turns to mush when small; photorealism or a plastic 3D render; text, letters, numbers or runes; drop shadows; anything see-through.

LAYOUT / SIZE — measured against the image, not judged by eye:
· Each box is centred in its 512 x 512 square and about 380 px wide (74% of the square) — as big as its grey box.
· At least 60 px of magenta between every box and its square's edges.

BACKGROUND — this matters more than the style.
Fill every pixel that is not art with solid, flat, pure magenta #FF00FF, edge to edge — treat it as a green screen.
· EXACTLY #FF00FF — red 255, green 0, blue 255. Not pink, not purple, not a tinted version of it.
· NOT transparent (never a grey-and-white checkerboard), NOT white, NOT a gradient, NOT a texture.
· No card, tile, plate, circle or frame behind any object; no grid lines or panel borders; no glow, halo or shadow on the magenta. Any glow stays INSIDE the object's outline.
· No object contains magenta or hot pink anywhere.

BEFORE YOU CALL IT FINISHED, count and check:

· No text, numbers, sparkle stars, panel borders or watermarks.

OUTPUT: one image, 1024 x 1024 pixels, 1:1 square, PNG. If your tool has an aspect-ratio control, set it to 1:1. No labels, captions, numbers or watermarks.
```
